Slots.maps_to: no sim counterpart (AXEBOTS_NORMAL = Encounter(id="axebots_normal", monster_classes=[Axebot]) -- axebot.py:92-95, `slots` left at its default `()`)
Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: AxebotsNormal.cs:11 declares `Slots => ["front"]`. Filed under shared mechanism `encounter/_slot_order` alongside `encounter/knights`'s slot-name gap. Traced to both readers of `Encounter.Slots`/`Creature.SlotName` on the game side: (1) `EncounterModel.GetNextSlot` (EncounterModel.cs:245-248), called from `Encounter.GetNextSlot(CombatState)` at the ONE site that reads it for this unit's content -- `StockPower.cs:24`'s respawn passes `base.Owner.SlotName` directly (not `GetNextSlot`), so this reader is not exercised by Axebot at all; (2) `CombatManager.AddCreature`'s `SortEnemiesBySlotName()` call, gated on `creature.SlotName != null` (per `audit/records/monster/fabricator.json`'s already-closed guard on the identical mechanism). AxebotsNormal has exactly one live enemy at any moment -- the original Axebot, or its one-at-a-time StockPower respawn, never both (StockPower.on_death fires only `!wasRemovalPrevented && target == base.Owner`, i.e. after the original is gone) -- so a resort of a one-element `Enemies` list is a no-op on the game side too. DORMANT, same conclusion `power/stock.json`'s own already-filed guard reaches for the respawn half of this exact fact ("a single-enemy replacement lands in the same list position either way", verdicted `waiver` there); this hook (`EncounterModel.Slots` itself, never previously verdicted anywhere) is the encounter-tier half of the same observable and is recorded here as a dormant `gap` rather than re-derived as a second `waiver`, since it is a genuinely un-ported declarative property, just one with zero live consequence for this unit.

HasScene.rationale: Presentation only -- gates whether the encounter loads a bespoke `.tscn` combat scene (AxebotsNormal.cs:13, `HasScene => true`; `scenes/encounters/axebots_normal.tscn` exists and declares a `front` Marker2D matching the `Slots` value). No scene loading in the headless sim.

RoomType.rationale: AxebotsNormal.cs:15 `RoomType => RoomType.Monster`. Modeled structurally by pool membership (`ActRooms.normal_keys`), matching. One shared mechanism across this batch; see `encounter/_room_type_and_weak` in the report.

AllPossibleMonsters.issue: AxebotsNormal.cs:17 returns a single-element list with `Axebot`. Shared finding, filed once under `encounter/_all_possible_monsters` (see `encounter/aeonglass` for the full enumeration of the three game-side debug/UI consumers -- none RNG- or combat-affecting; dormant because the headless sim has neither feature).

GenerateMonsters.rationale: ROSTER: AxebotsNormal.cs:19-22 returns exactly one `(Axebot, "front")` pair; `AXEBOTS_NORMAL = Encounter(id="axebots_normal", monster_classes=[Axebot])` (axebot.py:92-95) -- one monster, same class. ORDER: trivially matches. SLOT: diverges -- see the `Slots` hook above (filed there as the mechanism, since it is `Encounter.Slots`/`monster_slots` that is missing, and `GenerateMonsters`'s OWN list-order/roster/draw-count are otherwise exact). DRAW COUNT: zero on both sides -- `AxebotsNormal.GenerateMonsters` (AxebotsNormal.cs:19-22) never touches `base.Rng`, and the sim's fixed-composition path draws nothing (monsters/base.py:408-411).

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by AxebotsNormal. The sim's `Encounter` dataclass is never registered with `HookSystem` anywhere -- never a hook listener on either side.

guards.what: Draw count / stream independence of the per-encounter Rng
guards.rationale: Zero draws in GenerateMonsters (see above). The per-encounter Rng's independence is never exercised by this unit's initial roster.

guards.what: The Niche HP-roll, for the ONE unit in this batch with a genuine HP RANGE (min_hp=70, max_hp=78)
guards.rationale: Unlike the other eight units, Axebot's roll actually matters. `Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue` (Creature.cs:371-383) builds `hashSet = Range(70,9).ToHashSet()` (9 values, 70..78 inclusive), excludes siblings' HP (none, single enemy), and draws `rng.NextItem(hashSet)` -- one draw over the 9-candidate ascending set. The sim's `CombatState._roll_parity_hp` (combat.py:402-422) reads the CLASS bounds `Axebot.min_hp/max_hp` (not the instance's own already-overwritten legacy-roll value -- the method's own docstring at combat.py:409-412 explains why), builds the identical ascending `candidates` list, and draws `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))` -- one draw over the same 9-candidate set, matching order and count. Independently confirmed for the RESPAWN path too (StockPower.on_death -> `CreatureCmd.add` -> `combat.assign_parity_hp`, combat.py:438-446), per `audit/records/monster/axebot.json`'s guard "Reachability" and `audit/records/power/stock.json`'s guard on `combat._rng`/Niche, both already verdicted `faithful` -- not re-derived here, matched per rule 3.

rooms.py:265 lists `axebots` in Glory's `normal_keys`, and `AXEBOTS_NORMAL` is registered in `sts2_rl/monsters/glory/__init__.py`'s `ENCOUNTERS` dict (line 62). Reachable with fully ported content on both sides, including the StockPower respawn chain (`monster/axebot.json`, `power/stock.json`, both already audited).
